svg.text: Repair an expired separator before hinting its key
A separator is a copied reference to a child’s former minimum. Reclaiming key blocks can invalidate it while the child still holds live history. Its CV is checked
before any key hint; an expired separator is refreshed from the child, reading versions before bytes, so the old reference is never dereferenced.
A An expired separator over a live child
reclaimCV = 20. Separator rank 1, the boundary before L1, still names key block 5, reclaimed and reused; L1 has live entries.
reused: now a newer key block
4 only now: hint the key bytes of the new reference,
set CompareKeys, yield; the compare happens next visit
check the separator’s CV before issuing any key hint: 12 ≤ reclaimCV → expired; the reference is not followed
refresh from the child: a synchronous descent without prefetch, so this visit may stall; accepted rather than adding refresh states or touching every child
replace the reference and the CV in the separator with L1’s first live entry (mango, cv 31); L1 is queued for deferred cleanup; its expired entry is not compacted now
issue the key prefetch for the repaired reference and continue the partition at the next visit
B Every child of an internal node is empty, and live history lies in the next subtree
a long read [k, r) at RV 30 is routed through I4; none of its children has a live entry, but L7, under the next internal node, holds [p, q) @ 52
read [k, r) RV 30: routed conservatively left, lands in L4, scans right through the chain; [p, q) @ 52 > 30 → conflict
Marking: when the child has no live entry and no live neighbor to borrow from, every separator CV of I4 is set to EmptyChildCV and no old reference is read.
Routing: an empty marker is not a key. Partitioning treats it as above the current reads and narrows to the left; routing right could skip a live predecessor,
while the forward scan through the linked leaves recovers any live write to the right. A wholly empty subtree therefore never drops the read task.
Lifetime: I4 and its leaves stay allocated and linked while tasks may hold bounds or ranks there; they are released by the deferred cleanup after traversal.
Order of operations that keeps this safe
Versions before bytes: a CV is a plain integer in the node, a key is a reference into a block that may have been reused. Checking the CV first means the only
key bytes ever hinted or compared belong to a reference known to be live. Refreshing replaces the separator in place and leaves child entries where they are,
because other tasks may have saved bounds in the same node. The refresh descent is the one access in the read path that is not prefetched: a possible stall,
paid only when a separator about to be used has expired, which v2.6 chose over eager refresh of every expired separator.
